views.name: flights_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  flight_no,
  scheduled_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  departure_airport,
  arrival_airport,
  status,
  aircraft_code,
  actual_departure,
  actual_arrival
FROM flights
WHERE status IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized flight-level relation. Use this to analyze scheduled vs actual times, join to airports, aircrafts, tickets, or compute punctuality. Preserves original identifiers and casts timestamps to SQLite-compatible types if necessary. | Use for: flight punctuality (delays, on-time rates); flight-level joins to tickets/boarding passes; scheduling vs actual time analyses

views.name: flights_with_airports
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.flight_id,
  f.flight_no,
  f.scheduled_departure,
  f.scheduled_arrival,
  f.departure_airport,
  dep.airport_name AS airport_name_departure,
  dep.city AS city_departure,
  dep.coordinates AS coordinates_departure,
  dep.timezone AS timezone_departure,
  f.arrival_airport,
  arr.airport_name AS airport_name_arrival,
  arr.city AS city_arrival,
  arr.coordinates AS coordinates_arrival,
  arr.timezone AS timezone_arrival,
  f.status,
  f.aircraft_code,
  f.actual_departure,
  f.actual_arrival
FROM flights f
LEFT JOIN airports_data dep ON f.departure_airport = dep.airport_code
LEFT JOIN airports_data arr ON f.arrival_airport = arr.airport_code
views.description: Flight rows enriched with departure and arrival airport descriptive fields. Useful when questions need airport names, city, coordinates or timezone alongside flight schedule. Keeps flight_id grain. | Use for: routes and airport-level metrics; displaying flight schedule with airport names/cities/timezones; geospatial analyses using airport coordinates

views.name: ticket_flights_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticket_no,
  flight_id,
  fare_conditions,
  amount
FROM ticket_flights
views.description: Normalized ticket-flight leg records (one row per ticket leg). Use for fare/leg-level aggregations, joining to flights/bookings/tickets, and for calculating per-leg revenue. Preserves original identifiers and amount/fare attributes. | Use for: per-leg revenue and fare class analyses; join to flights to get schedule per ticket leg; summing ticket amounts across legs or bookings

views.name: tickets_with_bookings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.ticket_no,
  t.book_ref,
  b.book_date,
  b.total_amount,
  t.passenger_id
FROM tickets t
LEFT JOIN bookings b ON t.book_ref = b.book_ref
views.description: Tickets joined to their booking metadata. Use when questions need booking date or booking-level total_amount together with ticket/passenger identifiers. Grain is one row per ticket. | Use for: time-series of ticket issuance by booking date; revenue per booking vs per-ticket comparisons; passenger-level reporting with booking context

views.name: boarding_passes_with_seats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bp.ticket_no,
  bp.flight_id,
  bp.boarding_no,
  bp.seat_no,
  s.aircraft_code AS aircraft_code,
  s.fare_conditions AS fare_conditions_seatmap
FROM boarding_passes bp
LEFT JOIN seats s ON bp.seat_no = s.seat_no
views.description: Boarding passes enriched with seat map fare_conditions for the aircraft model. Useful to validate seat assignments against expected fare class for that aircraft type. Grain: one row per boarding pass (ticket_no + flight_id + boarding_no). | Use for: seat assignment vs fare class validation; list of assigned seats per flight; seat map completeness checks

views.name: booking_revenue_by_booking
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.book_ref,
  SUM(tf.amount) AS total_amount_from_legs,
  COUNT(DISTINCT t.ticket_no) AS ticket_count,
  COUNT(tf.flight_id) AS leg_count
FROM tickets t
LEFT JOIN ticket_flights tf ON t.ticket_no = tf.ticket_no
GROUP BY t.book_ref
views.description: Aggregate revenue at booking level by summing associated ticket_flights.amount. Use to compare booking.total_amount with sum of leg fares, detect mismatches, or compute booking-level revenue metrics. Grain: one row per book_ref. | Use for: reconciling booking total_amount vs component leg amounts; average legs per booking or tickets per booking; identifying multi-leg or multi-ticket bookings

views.name: flight_passenger_manifest
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tf.ticket_no,
  tf.flight_id,
  tf.fare_conditions AS fare_conditions_leg,
  tf.amount,
  t.book_ref,
  t.passenger_id,
  bp.boarding_no,
  bp.seat_no
FROM ticket_flights tf
LEFT JOIN tickets t ON tf.ticket_no = t.ticket_no
LEFT JOIN boarding_passes bp ON tf.ticket_no = bp.ticket_no AND tf.flight_id = bp.flight_id
views.description: Per-flight passenger manifest built by joining ticket_flights -> tickets -> boarding_passes. Useful to get which passengers/tickets are associated with a flight and their seat assignments. Grain: one row per ticket leg on a flight (ticket_no + flight_id). | Use for: manifest for a given flight_id; seat occupancy and passenger lists per flight; revenue per passenger per flight

views.name: aircrafts_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  aircraft_code,
  model,
  range
FROM aircrafts_data
views.description: One row per aircraft type (aircraft_code) with descriptive model and range. Use when joining to flights or summarizing by aircraft type. | Use for: fleet composition by model; range-based route capability analyses; join to flights to get aircraft model per flight

views.name: flight_with_aircraft
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.flight_id,
  f.flight_no,
  f.scheduled_departure,
  f.scheduled_arrival,
  f.departure_airport,
  f.arrival_airport,
  f.status,
  f.aircraft_code,
  a.model AS model,
  a.range AS range,
  f.actual_departure,
  f.actual_arrival
FROM flights f
LEFT JOIN aircrafts_data a ON f.aircraft_code = a.aircraft_code
views.description: Flights enriched with aircraft descriptive attributes (model and range). Useful for per-flight analyses that need aircraft capabilities or labels. Grain: one row per flight_id. | Use for: assigning aircraft model to flights; route suitability by aircraft range; fleet utilization per model

views.name: tickets_count_by_booking
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.book_ref,
  COUNT(DISTINCT t.ticket_no) AS ticket_count,
  SUM(tf.amount) AS total_leg_amount
FROM tickets t
LEFT JOIN ticket_flights tf ON t.ticket_no = tf.ticket_no
GROUP BY t.book_ref
views.description: Counts tickets and sums leg amounts per booking. Useful to profile bookings by ticket count and revenue. Grain: one row per book_ref. | Use for: booking composition and revenue; identifying single-ticket vs multi-ticket bookings; comparing booking.total_amount to summed legs
